summary.text: Katy Padilla Stout is the Democratic nominee for this open border-area seat. She is an attorney and former elementary school teacher who, according to her campaign website, practices child welfare and education law at a family firm in Carrizo Springs. She won the March 3, 2026 Democratic primary with 52.1% of the vote in a four-candidate field.

paragraphs.text: Describes herself as a lifelong Texan raised by a single mother; says her father and grandparents were migrant farmworkers from South Texas.
Graduated from Lee High School in San Antonio and earned a bachelor's degree from the University of Texas at Austin, in education according to her campaign website.
Taught elementary school in Northside ISD before attending law school.

Earned a law degree from the South Texas College of Law and built a practice focused on child welfare and education law; she says she now works with her father at their family firm based in Carrizo Springs.

Has served since 2017 as an appointed member of the Bexar County Child Welfare Board and sits on the board of directors of Artvango Therapeutic Services, a nonprofit that provides expressive therapies for children.
Says she lives in San Antonio with her husband, a career prosecutor, and their four children, two of whom they adopted through foster care.
Won the March 3, 2026 Democratic primary with 52.1% of the vote over Santos Limon, Bruce Richardson and Gretel Marysdatter Enck.
